tenNotes: It rained heavily all afternoon and the streets flooded a bit.
The forecast says sunny skies for the rest of the week.
A cold front is moving in, temperatures will drop tonight.
I tried a new pasta recipe tonight and it turned out great.
The bread didn't rise properly, might be the old yeast.
Grilled the chicken a bit too long, it was slightly dry.
The new laptop takes forever to boot up, might need a factory reset.
Finally fixed the bug that was crashing the app on startup.
Upgraded my phone's storage but it's still running slow.
My favorite hiking trail closes for the winter next month.
input.eleventhNote: The wifi router keeps dropping the connection every hour.
input.note: Fixed 10 topically-mixed notes (weather/cooking/tech/other, deliberately not a single tight topic, so PCA has real structure to find), then an 11th added. Measured: refit project() over all 10 notes' chunks, record each note centroid's pixel position via the SAME fitProjectionToViewport/projectToViewportPixels transform Map.tsx renders with (600x600 viewport, 40px padding) -- then refit over all 11 notes' chunks, re-read the ORIGINAL 10 notes' pixel positions under the new fit, and measure per-note Euclidean pixel displacement. The measured mean (252px) is large relative to the 600px canvas -- confirmed not a bug: with only 10-11 points, refitting PCA genuinely can rotate the axes and (via the viewport's own auto-scaling to fit the new extremum) rescale everything, both of which are real effects a visitor actually sees on screen, which is exactly why SPEC.md's disclosure exists ('position is relative... will shift as you add or remove notes; it is not a fixed or absolute measurement').

assertion: Re-fitting the PCA projection after adding one note to a fixed 10-note set, then re-reading the original 10 notes' pixel positions (same viewport transform as the live map), produces a measured mean displacement and max displacement within a small tolerance of the pinned values below -- if the chunking, embedding, or PCA algorithm ever changes enough to move these numbers meaningfully, this assertion fails loudly rather than letting the on-page copy (which reads this same file's pinned meanDisplacementPx) go stale. Re-running the whole measurement twice on the identical 10-note input produces byte-identical centroid coordinates (determinism).
